items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: the gentleman at that time that was leader, when I got into the orchestra, was a Mr. Clarence Hart$

ctx.x: I understand. And the band that he was playing in was the Imperial Jazz Band?

The Imperial Jazz Band. That was a very popular band in Lake Charles and the gentleman at that time that was leader, when I got into the orchestra, was a Mr. Clarence Hart$, and Mr. Hart$ was a very marvelous saxophone player, he played all of the saxophones, but I think his basic instrument was the tenor saxophone. No, not the tenor, I'm sorry, the alto, he was an alto man. And he and my father and Tony Babbins and Bunk Johnson, the late Bunk Johnson was

a friend of my dad's, incidentally. They knew each other down in that area where my father was born. I think Bunk came from a little town called New Iberia, if I'm not mistaken.* If he wasn't born there he stayed in New Iberia quite awhile, but that's where he and my father knew each other, and of course when Bunk Johnson came up to Lake Charles, then he played in the Imperial Orchestra, and I -- this is the one thing that I really -- I didn't realize naturally at the time, I didn't even think, I don't think…
